data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference constitutes a performative contradiction where Popper acts exactly as an inductivist would when choosing a well-corroborated bridge design, relying on the implicit premise that past survival indicates future stability.","counterconditions":[{"case":"refuted if a coherent account can be provided where preferring a better-corroborated theory is justified solely as a method to maximize the severity of future tests without any assumption that the theory will actually succeed","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"refuted if a definitive textual analysis of Popper's distinction between 'rational preference' based on critical scrutiny versus 'inductive inference' based on probability assignments is provided","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"refuted if clarification shows that 'rational preference' in Popper's framework relies solely on the logical asymmetry between verification and falsification","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"No amount of semantic maneuvering around 'corroboration' vs. 'probability' can mask the fact that acting on corroboration requires an inductive leap, causing Popper's system to collapse into crypto-induction whenever it leaves abstract methodology.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
